raw_case_text: A 19-year-old male presented to our medical clinic in mid-2009 with complaints of acne, hair loss, and difficulty in getting up from sitting position with evidence of proximal muscle weakness. He had been recently diagnosed with dermatomyositis based on his clinical features of elevated creatine kinase levels, typical skin changes, and electromyography (EMG) pattern consistent with dermatomyositis. His medications at the time included prednisone, methotrexate, folate, and vitamin D. He was sexually active with both male and female partners with inconsistent use of condoms. Subsequently, he had multiple clinic visits between 2010 and 2011 for complaints of sore throat, fever, chills, anal pain, anal itching, and anal discharge. During this time, he was treated for oral candidiasis, scabies infestation, syphilis, and condyloma acuminata. He refused HIV testing, claiming that he was tested negative elsewhere. In early 2012, he consented for HIV testing. HIV ELISA and western blot were positive, with a CD4+ cell count of 182 cells/microL and HIV RNA copies of 1,337,310 copies/mL on diagnosis. He was started on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART). After initiation of HAART his CD4+ count gradually increased to 346 cells/microL and HIV-1 RNA copies decreased to 462 copies/mL within 2 months. At this time, he started having frequent flares of dermatomyositis. His dermatomyositis had been fairly well controlled on prednisone and methotrexate before initiation of HAART. He was switched to a combination of prednisone and azathioprine, then with mycophenolate mofetil, all with poor response. In June 2013, he was started on monthly intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIG), to which he initially had a fair response but ultimately required reintroduction of methotrexate and increased doses of prednisone to control the dermatomyositis flares. Despite this regimen, he had another dermatomyositis flare in 2014. In mid-2015, he presented to the emergency department with complains of diffuse muscle pain, chest pain, and shortness of breath on exertion. His last dose of IVIG was a week before presentation. His active medications were prednisone 60 mg daily, methotrexate 40 mg once a week, IVIG once a month, and Atripla. On physical examination, he had mild heliotrope rash on eyes, chest wall tenderness, neck, and proximal muscle weakness on both upper and lower limbs. Critical laboratory findings included creatine kinase of 1,145 IU/L, aspartate transaminase of 400 IU/L, and alanine transaminase of 220 IU/L. Because of the refractoriness of therapy, a muscle biopsy was done which confirmed the clinical diagnosis of dermatomyositis (Fig. 1a and 1b). He was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone at stress doses with prompt improvement in overall muscle strength. He was discharged to follow up as an outpatient for rituximab therapy. He continues to take HAART and follows up in Infectious disease clinic. At the time of this report, the patient's latest helper CD4 counts was 320 cells/mcL and HIV-1 ultrasensitive RNA <20 copies/mL 02/8/2016. The patient is yet to follow up at the rheumatology clinic.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 19-year-old male with dermatomyositis and subsequently diagnosed HIV-1 infection presented with recurrent refractory dermatomyositis flares (proximal muscle weakness, diffuse myalgias, heliotrope rash, chest pain, and exertional dyspnea) following antiretroviral-induced immune reconstitution.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with dermatomyositis in mid-2009 (well controlled initially on oral prednisone and methotrexate), the patient had multiple visits in 2010–2011 for oral candidiasis, scabies, syphilis, and anal condylomata before consenting to HIV testing in early 2012. Within 2 months of starting HAART (Atripla), as his CD4+ count rose from 182 to 346 cells/µL and HIV-1 RNA fell from 1,337,310 to 462 copies/mL, he began experiencing frequent severe flares of dermatomyositis refractory to azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, monthly IVIG, methotrexate (40 mg weekly), and high-dose prednisone (60 mg daily), culminating in a mid-2015 emergency department admission for diffuse myalgia, chest pain, and exertional dyspnea.
subjective.past_medical_history: Dermatomyositis diagnosed in mid-2009; HIV-1 infection diagnosed in early 2012; history of oral candidiasis, scabies, syphilis, and perianal condyloma acuminata in 2010–2011. Sexual history notable for inconsistent condom use with male and female partners.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for diffuse muscle pain, proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope eyelid rash, chest pain, and exertional dyspnea. Home medications in mid-2015: efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir (Atripla), prednisone 60 mg daily, methotrexate 40 mg weekly, monthly IVIG, folate, and vitamin D.

objective.physical_examination: Mid-2015 emergency department examination revealed a mild bilateral periorbital heliotrope rash, anterior chest wall tenderness, and symmetric neck flexor and bilateral upper and lower extremity proximal muscle weakness.
objective.routine_investigations: Mid-2015 flare labs demonstrated markedly elevated serum creatine kinase (CK 1,145 IU/L), AST 400 IU/L, and ALT 220 IU/L. Baseline electromyography (EMG) in 2009 had shown a classic myopathic/inflammatory dermatomyositis pattern.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count was 182 cells/µL at HIV diagnosis in early 2012, rose to 346 cells/µL within 2 months of HAART initiation, and was 320 cells/µL in February 2016. Skeletal muscle biopsy performed in mid-2015 confirmed active dermatomyositis with perifascicular atrophy and inflammatory myopathy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Autoimmune immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) manifesting as severe, treatment-refractory exacerbations of pre-existing dermatomyositis following HAART-induced CD4+ T-cell recovery (CD4+ rising from 182 to 346 cells/µL and HIV-1 RNA suppressed from 1,337,310 to <20 copies/mL on Atripla, confirmed by positive HIV ELISA, Western blot, and 2015 skeletal muscle biopsy). The acute mid-2015 flare was treated with stress-dose intravenous methylprednisolone with prompt recovery of muscle strength, and the patient was discharged on continued HAART (HIV-1 RNA <20 copies/mL, CD4+ count 320 cells/µL) with planned outpatient rituximab therapy.
